audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Olaf's W 'Vicious Strikes' and attributes his lifesteal to it, in whys[1], whys[3], whys[5], spikes[0], spikes[3], mid, late and wants.foe[1]. Both the name and the effect are wrong.
audit.why: Riot's kit for this patch: W is Tough It Out — 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield', cooldown 16/15/14/13/12. There is no lifesteal on it. His sustain comes from the passive, Berserker Rage — 'Olaf gains Attack Speed and Life Steal based on his missing Health' — which is a materially different fact for the player: the healing SCALES UP as you push him low, so the last third of his health bar is the hardest part, and a burst that fails to kill leaves him stronger, not weaker. Advice written around 'W lifesteal' tells the player to trade around a 16-second cooldown that does not gate the healing at all.
audit.corrected: W is Tough It Out (attack speed plus a shield, 16s at rank 1). The lifesteal is Berserker Rage, the passive, and it grows with his missing health.
sources: enemyKit P and W Riot text

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'mid' refers to 'the True Grit armor and Bushwhack stats you stacked all lane'.
audit.why: Graves has no ability called Bushwhack. Riot's E is Quickdraw — 'dashes forward gaining an Armor and Magic Resist boost... gain two stacks of True Grit'. The resist stacking has exactly one name and this invents a second one alongside it.
audit.corrected: Removed; the resists are True Grit from Quickdraw.

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'early' says his Q (Undertow) 'slows you and chunks true damage'.
audit.why: Undertow is not true damage. Riot: 'throws an axe into the ground at a target location, dealing damage to enemies it passes through and reducing their Armor and Move Speed. If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset.' The true damage is Reckless Swing (E). Conflating them hides the actually decisive Undertow property — the ARMOR REDUCTION, which strips the True Grit resists Graves' whole kit is built on, from 1000 range on a 9-second cooldown that resets entirely on pickup.
audit.corrected: Undertow slows and reduces armor at 1000 range, 9s, resetting on pickup; Reckless Swing (325 range, 11/10/9/8/7s) is the true damage.
sources: enemyKit Q and E Riot text, ranges and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is called a blind in wants.you[1], early, mid, whys[2], whys[4], spikes[0], spikes[1] and report[10].t.
audit.why: Riot: 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' Nearsight plus an impact slow, no blind. It matters more than usual here because the text tells the player to 'W-blind him to stop his autos' against a champion whose passive gives him attack speed — the plan does not exist.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen slows on impact and cuts sight range; it does not stop his attacks.
sources: ownerKit W Riot text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Content win[] and the full-layer phases both read Graves / Skill / Olaf / Olaf / Graves / Olaf / Olaf, against a packet levelChart of Olaf / Skill / Skill / Olaf / Olaf / Olaf / Olaf and a 36.36% win rate. The lane is also tagged EVEN at difficulty 5.5/10.
audit.why: The content whys agree with the packet, not with the enums beside them: whys[0] opens 'He owns level 1', whys[2] says the axe loop 'keeps it close' (Skill), and whys[4] calls Level 6 'his single best window to all-in'. Rows 0, 2 and 4 are wrong in both layers. A 36.36% lane where the enemy owns five of seven stages is not an even matchup.
audit.corrected: Both charts set to Olaf / Skill / Skill / Olaf / Olaf / Olaf / Olaf, ratings 3,5,5,3,2,3,2; diff HARD, difficulty 8/10, Olaf carry threat 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] gives Level 6 to Graves at 7/10 with the generic Collateral Damage line; the content layer correctly calls it Olaf's best window.
audit.why: Ragnarok is 100/90/80s and, per Riot, 'passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking.' Both halves work against Graves — the passive resists blunt the shell burst before the ultimate is ever pressed.
audit.corrected: Level 6 flipped to Olaf at 2/10 and rewritten around Ragnarok's real numbers.

Pair that with E (Reckless Swing) true damage and a Q that reduces your armor, and the True Grit resists you stacked all lane are exactly what his all-in walks through.

edits.before: You do not win the straight duel here. An itemized Olaf with R up is CC-immune and out-sustains your DPS with W lifesteal, while his E (Reckless Swing) and Q axe true damage shred through everything your armor-and-MR stacking builds toward. Use your E mobility and R (Collateral Damage) as escape and pick tools, not as engage into him. Sidestep his axes, farm your reload tempo, and look to roam and skirmish elsewhere as a mobile carry rather than trying to solo a champion whose CC-immune all-in ignores your tank stats.

notes: Biggest find: the content layer calls Olaf's W 'Vicious Strikes' and hangs his entire sustain on it, in eight separate fields. On this patch W is Tough It Out — attack speed plus a SHIELD, 16/15/14/13/12s — and it has no healing at all. The lifesteal is the passive, Berserker Rage, scaling with his MISSING health. That is not a cosmetic name fix: it inverts the trading advice, because the healing gets stronger as he gets lower rather than being gated behind a 16-second button. 'Bushwhack stats' appeared again in content mid (Graves' E is Quickdraw, the resists are True Grit) and Undertow was described as true damage when the true damage is Reckless Swing — Undertow's real property, armor reduction at 1000 range on a 9s cooldown that fully resets on pickup, is the one that actually beats Graves and was nowhere in the text. Smoke Screen was called a blind in eight places; corrected. UNVERIFIED, left alone deliberately: several full-layer fields describe Graves' R as a 'disengage knockback' / 'peel knockback' (dosFull[2].t, phases[4] as written, breakdown.late) and the content layer built advice on Ragnarok blanking that knockback. Riot's R text says only 'dealing heavy damage to the first champion it hits... explodes dealing damage in a cone' — the only knockback in the kit text is the passive's, and it applies to NON-champions. I did not assert either way; I rewrote the fields I touched so they no longer depend on it, and left dosFull[2].t and breakdown.late untouched. Same caution for Undertow's 'grounding' derived flag, which Riot's description does not support — no advice here relies on it. Mirror file olaf__graves did not exist at audit time.
